# Espresso extraction

Good espresso is a 1:2 ratio in 25–30 seconds: 18g of coffee in, ~36g of
liquid out. Everything else is adjusting variables to hit that window.

## Dialing in

1. Fix the dose (18g) and grind one variable at a time.
2. Shot runs fast (< 20s) and tastes sour → grind finer.
3. Shot chokes (> 35s) and tastes bitter → grind coarser.
4. Only change one thing per shot, and log it: grind setting, time, yield, taste.

## Water and temperature

Use filtered water — scale kills machines faster than anything. 93°C is the
starting point; lighter roasts often like 94–95°C, dark roasts prefer 90–92°C
to avoid ashy bitterness.

## Milk

For a flat white, steam to ~55–60°C with glossy microfoam — the milk should
look like wet paint. Pour from low to mix, then close to the surface for
the art. If it screeches, the wand is too deep; if it glugs, it's too shallow.
